## AgentEvent
<!-- agent: yes -->

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent`

A single event from the agent loop.

Reference: SUBPHASE-0.0.md, "5. Agent Events" section.
Reference: docs/SUBMISSION-LIFECYCLE.md, "Provenance on events" (phase 2).

### args

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.args: dict[str, Any] | None`

Tool execution arguments (tool_execution_start)

### attempt

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.attempt: int | None`

Which retry a ``provider_retry`` announces, from 1.

### blocked

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.blocked: bool`

Whether a ``tool_execution_end`` is an extension VETO (S50) —
distinct from a generic errored result, so a front-end can render
"⛔ blocked by <ext>: <reason>" rather than a plain error box.

### blocked_by

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.blocked_by: str | None`

The extension that vetoed the call (its runner path label),
paired with ``blocked`` on a ``tool_execution_end``; ``None`` otherwise.

### close_reason

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.close_reason: SuspensionCloseReason | None`

On ``suspension_closed``, why it closed
(:data:`SuspensionCloseReason`). ``None`` on every other type.

### correlation

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.correlation: dict[str, Any] | None`

The submission's free-form origin detail (bus subject, cron
id, HTTP request id), carried through unchanged so an embedded server
can fan out to the right stream. ``None`` alongside ``submission_id``
(an EMPTY dict would claim "a submission with no correlation data";
``None`` says "no submission stamped this event" instead).

### cursor_id

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.cursor_id: str | None`

The :class:`~tau_agent_core.cursor.Cursor` whose turn emitted
this event. Several cursors run turns on one session at once, so a
renderer routes by it (docs/CURSORS.md §6). ``None`` outside a turn.

### delay_seconds

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.delay_seconds: float | None`

How long τ waits before re-sending it; the status being
retried is ``error_detail.status`` (docs/PROVIDER-RETRY.md §5).

### delta

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.delta: str | None`

One text fragment of a side completion, on
``side_completion_update``. ``None`` elsewhere.

### details

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.details: dict[str, Any] | None`

A tool's structured facts about its own execution on
``tool_execution_end`` — the path it read, the line range, the match
count, the diff. What ``result`` holds is what the MODEL reads; this
is what a head can render beside it. ``None`` when the tool declared
none, and on every other event type.

### dropped

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.dropped: list[str] | None`

The texts a user abort discarded, on ``follow_ups_dropped``
only: queued followUps, then waiting ``enqueue`` submissions
(docs/TURN-SETTINGS.md §5, §5.1). Written nowhere else.

### end_reason

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.end_reason: AgentEndReason | None`

How an ``agent_end`` closed, as one of ``"done"``,
``"terminate"``, ``"aborted"``, ``"max_turns"``,
``"repeat_tool_calls"``, ``"error"`` or ``"suspended"`` (the turn
unwound at a suspension, docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §3.2.2). ``None`` on
every other event type. This distinguishes a loop that finished from one that was cut
short: before it, a run stopped by ``max_turns`` emitted the same
``agent_end`` as one where the model simply had nothing more to say,
so a caller could not tell a truncated answer from a complete one.

### error

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.error: str | None`

Why an ``agent_end`` closed, when the loop raised rather than
finishing (``"RuntimeError: Connection refused"``). ``None`` on a
normal close; always paired with ``is_error=True``. On a
``provider_retry`` it is the failure being retried, with
``is_error=False`` because the turn goes on.

### error_detail

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.error_detail: ErrorDetail | None`

``error`` as fields (:class:`ErrorDetail`), set exactly
when ``error`` is, so a handler branches on a status or a class name
instead of parsing the string.

### is_error

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.is_error: bool`

Whether this event represents an error

### lock_holder

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.lock_holder: dict[str, Any] | None`

On ``lock_changed``, the process holding the tree's lock
(``LockHolder.to_dict``), or ``None``.

### max_retries

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.max_retries: int | None`

The most retries that request will make.

### message

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.message: dict[str, Any] | None`

Message data (agent_start/end, message_*)

### messages

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.messages: list[dict[str, Any]] | None`

List of messages produced (agent_end)

### parent_tool_call_id

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.parent_tool_call_id: str | None`

On a ``tool_execution_*`` event for a call a tool
made (``ctx.execute_tool``), the calling tool's call id. ``None`` for
a call the model made. Experimental.

### purpose

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.purpose: SideCompletionPurpose | None`

Which side completion a ``side_completion_*`` event reports —
``"compaction"`` or ``"branch_summary"``. ``None`` on every other
type. Side work belongs to no turn and stamps no ``submission_id``,
so this is what a renderer keys on instead.

### read_only

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.read_only: bool | None`

On ``lock_changed``, whether this process may no longer
write the head cursor's tree.

### reason

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.reason: SideCompletionReason | None`

What asked for it — ``"manual"``, ``"threshold"`` or
``"navigate"``. Set on all three ``side_completion_*`` events, so a
reader that joins late still learns whether the compaction it is
watching was requested or imposed. ``None`` on every other type.

### resolution

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.resolution: dict[str, Any] | None`

On ``suspension_closed``, what ``api.suspend`` returned:
``{id, action, values, answered_by, at_ms}``.

### response_headers

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.response_headers: dict[str, str] | None`

The HTTP response headers of the completion a
``message_end`` closes, names lowercased. Set only on the
usage-bearing ``message_end``; None there when the transport did not
capture them, and ``{}`` when the server sent none. Not persisted:
the message in the session log never carries them.

### result

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.result: Any | None`

Tool execution result (tool_execution_*)

### source

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.source: SubmissionSource | None`

The submission's origin (``"interactive"``, ``"bus"``, ``"agent"``,
…) — pi's ``InputSource`` equivalent, so a renderer can decide *how* to
show a turn (Jupyter's rule: render every source, differently) without
the core knowing any renderer exists. ``None`` alongside
``submission_id``.

### submission_id

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.submission_id: str | None`

The ``Submission`` that drove this turn, if any — Jupyter's
``parent_header``. ``None`` for a turn not driven through ``submit()``
(e.g. ``continue_conversation()``, which predates the Submission
contract) — an honest "no submission", never a fabricated id.

### submitter

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.submitter: str | None`

WHO submitted — an extension name, ``"human"``, a channel id.
``None`` alongside ``submission_id``.

### suspension

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.suspension: dict[str, Any] | None`

On ``suspension_open`` and ``suspension_closed``, the
suspension's state (:meth:`~tau_agent_core.suspensions.Suspension.state`):
its id, cursor and owner linkage, spec, site and whether it is
queued. ``suspension_open`` is sent again, ``queued`` false, when a
queued one reaches the front of its cursor's queue.

### text

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.text: str | None`

The finished side-completion text, on ``side_completion_end``.
Sent whole as well as in fragments, because a subscriber that
attached late or dropped a delta must still be able to render the
result rather than a partial one. ``None`` elsewhere, and ``None``
on an end that failed — paired with ``is_error`` and ``error``.

### timestamp

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.timestamp: int`

Milliseconds since epoch

### tool_call_id

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.tool_call_id: str | None`

Tool call ID (tool_*)

### tool_name

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.tool_name: str | None`

Tool name (tool_*)

### tool_results

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.tool_results: list[dict[str, Any]] | None`

List of tool result messages (turn_end)

### turn_index

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.turn_index: int | None`

Turn number (turn_*)

### type

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.type: Literal['agent_start', 'agent_end', 'turn_start', 'turn_end', 'message_start', 'message_update', 'message_end', 'tool_execution_start', 'tool_execution_update', 'tool_execution_end', 'side_completion_start', 'side_completion_update', 'side_completion_end', 'provider_retry', 'follow_ups_dropped', 'suspension_open', 'suspension_closed', 'lock_changed']`

Event type discriminator

### usage

`tau_agent_core.events.AgentEvent.usage: dict[str, int] | None`

What a side completion SPENT, on ``side_completion_end``. This is
the only place those tokens are observable: the work runs outside the
agent loop, so no ``turn_end`` counts it (docs/STREAMING-SIDE-WORK.md).

## ErrorDetail
<!-- agent: yes -->

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail`

A failure as fields, beside the ``error`` string on ``agent_end`` and ``provider_retry``.

See docs/RESPONSE-HEADERS.md §5.

### headers

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.headers: dict[str, str] | None`

The refusal's response headers, names lowercased; None when
none were captured, which includes every failure that is not an HTTP
refusal.

### key_sent

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.key_sent: bool | None`

A ``ProviderHttpError``'s ``key_sent``: whether the request
carried a key, which tells "no API key" from "API key refused" on a
401; None when not an HTTP refusal or the provider did not say.

### of

```python
of(exc: BaseException) -> 'ErrorDetail'
```

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.of`

The detail for ``exc``.

**Parameters**

- `exc: BaseException` — The exception that ended the loop or was retried.

**Returns**

Every field filled for a ``ProviderHttpError``; ``type`` and ``retryable`` for a ``ProviderConnectionError``, plus ``status`` for a ``ProviderStreamError`` whose frame named an HTTP-like code; ``type`` alone for anything else.

### retry_after

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.retry_after: float | None`

Seconds the server asked the client to wait, parsed from
``Retry-After``; None when it sent none or this is not an HTTP refusal.

### retryable

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.retryable: bool | None`

Whether ``tau_llm.retry.DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY`` counts this
failure as transient: True for a retryable status or a connection
failure, False for any other HTTP refusal and for a
``ProviderStreamError``, None for an exception τ makes no
transience judgement about. On ``agent_end`` a True means
τ's own retries ran out, or the server asked for a longer wait than
τ will make inside a turn.

### status

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.status: int | None`

The HTTP status of a ``ProviderHttpError``, or the HTTP-like
code a ``ProviderStreamError``'s frame named; None otherwise.

### type

`tau_agent_core.events.ErrorDetail.type: str`

The exception's class name, e.g. ``"ProviderHttpError"``. Always set.

## EventBus
<!-- agent: yes -->

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus`

Central event bus for τ-agent-core.

Provides publish/subscribe for AgentEvents. Used by:
- AgentSession (for TUI consumers)
- AgentLoop (for emitting events)
- Extensions (for event-driven behavior)

Reference: SUBPHASE-0.0.md, "5. Agent Events" section.
Reference: PHASE-3-SUBPHASE-0.md EventBus contract.

Constraint: "fire-and-forget" is a failure-isolation contract, not a
scheduling one — see the module docstring. ``emit`` awaits each handler
that returns a coroutine before moving to the next, so handlers are
ordered with respect to each other AND to the emitter, and a handler that
suspends suspends the emitter. Subscribers rely on this to pace the agent
loop; do not "optimize" it into ``create_task``.

**Contract**

class EventBus:
    def on(self, channel: str, handler: Callable) -> Callable[[], None]: ...
    def off(self, channel: str, handler: Callable) -> None: ...
    async def emit(self, event: AgentEvent) -> None: ...
    async def emit_channel(self, channel: str, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None: ...

### emit

```python
async emit(event: AgentEvent) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.emit`

Emit an event to all matching handlers.

Handlers subscribed to the specific event type, then those on 'all',
receive the event, each awaited in turn. They run outside any hook
dispatch, so none inherits ``api.suspend``'s permission
(docs/STEP-DEBUGGER.md §3.2).

**Parameters**

- `event: AgentEvent` — The AgentEvent to emit.

### emit_channel

```python
async emit_channel(channel: str, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.emit_channel`

Emit to all handlers on a specific channel.

A handler that raises is surfaced and the rest still run, except for a
:class:`~tau_agent_core.policies.HandlerPolicyError` (a policed ``ext:``
handler's ``Failed``), which propagates to the emitter at once. An
``ext:`` channel's handlers run in the emitter's hook dispatch, so they
may ``api.suspend`` where it may; every other channel's run outside it.

**Parameters**

- `channel: str` — Channel name.
- `*args: Any` — Positional arguments passed to each handler.
- `**kwargs: Any` — Keyword arguments passed to each handler.

**Raises**

- `HandlerPolicyError` — a policed handler failed.

### has_listeners

```python
has_listeners(channel: str) -> bool
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.has_listeners`

Whether anyone is subscribed to ``channel``.

For a caller deciding whether an un-deliverable emit is a problem: a
synchronous appender with no running loop cannot dispatch, and that is
only a lost event if something was waiting for it.

**Parameters**

- `channel: str` — Channel name. ``"all"`` subscribers are not counted — they take :meth:`emit`'s ``AgentEvent`` stream, not a named channel.

**Returns**

True if at least one handler is registered on ``channel``.

### off

```python
off(channel: str, handler: Callable) -> None
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.off`

Remove a specific handler from a channel.

**Parameters**

- `channel: str` — Channel name.
- `handler: Callable` — The handler to remove.

### on

```python
on(channel: str, handler: Callable) -> Callable[[], None]
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.on`

Subscribe to a channel.

**Parameters**

- `channel: str` — Channel name (e.g., 'all', 'agent_start').
- `handler: Callable` — Callable that receives an AgentEvent.

**Returns**

An unsubscribe function.

**Example**

>>> bus = EventBus()
>>> def my_handler(event):
...     print(event.type)
>>> unsub = bus.on('all', my_handler)
>>> await bus.emit(AgentEvent(type='agent_start', timestamp=0))
>>> unsub()  # Remove subscription

### on_error

```python
on_error(listener: ErrorListener) -> Callable[[], None]
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.on_error`

Register a listener for exceptions raised by this bus's handlers.

S44 (anchor G3). A handler that raises is routed here instead of being
swallowed; the session binds this to the same on_error surface the
:class:`~tau_agent_core.extensions.runner.ExtensionRunner` uses. With no
listener bound, the error goes to stderr.

**Parameters**

- `listener: ErrorListener` — Called with ``(error, channel)``.

**Returns**

A callable that removes ``listener``; calling it twice is harmless.

### subscribers

```python
subscribers(channel: str) -> tuple[Callable[..., Any], ...]
```

`tau_agent_core.events.EventBus.subscribers`

A snapshot of ``channel``'s handlers, in subscription order.

**Parameters**

- `channel: str` — Channel name; ``"all"`` subscribers are not included.

**Returns**

The handlers; an api's ``ext:`` subscription is a :class:`ChannelSubscriber`.

## follow_ups_dropped_notice
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
follow_ups_dropped_notice(event: dict[str, Any]) -> str
```

`tau_agent_core.follow_ups.follow_ups_dropped_notice`

The line a head shows for a ``follow_ups_dropped`` event or its wire payload.

**Parameters**

- `event: dict[str, Any]` — ``AgentEvent.model_dump()`` or a ``WireEvent`` dict; reads ``dropped``.

**Returns**

One line, e.g. ``"Aborted: dropped 1 queued follow-up: 'continue on the cheap model'"``. Each text is cut at 40 characters with ``…``; the event keeps it whole.

## retry_notice
<!-- agent: yes -->

```python
retry_notice(event: dict[str, Any]) -> str
```

`tau_agent_core.provider_retry.retry_notice`

The line a head shows for a ``provider_retry`` event or its wire payload.

Example: ``"HTTP 503 from model 'q' at 'http://h': loading — retry 1 of 3 in 1.2s"``.

**Parameters**

- `event: dict[str, Any]` — A ``provider_retry`` payload: ``AgentEvent.model_dump()`` or a ``WireEvent`` dict. Reads ``error``, ``attempt``, ``max_retries`` and ``delay_seconds``.

**Returns**

``"<error> — retry <attempt> of <max_retries> in <delay>s"``, the delay to one decimal place.

**Raises**

- `KeyError` — If the payload lacks one of them, i.e. is not a ``provider_retry``.
